items.title: Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1957-04-20
items.q: He said, but I'd like to have you to work with me. I tell you sound very good.

ctx.x: You just walked him down the street, you remember?

Yeah. Uh, Jackson and... and Roberson Street. Uh-huh. I was on Jackson, and he heard the horn, and he stopped, and he rapped on the door. I came to the serial man, he said, are you going to trombone? I said, yeah. Yes, sir. He said, well, you know who I am? I said, I don't really. He said, I'm the king. I said, king who? He said, Bolden. I said, no, hey, Mr. Bolden. He said, uh, you live here? I said, no, not exactly. My sister lives here. I live out in the country. He said, but I'd like to have you to work with…
Oh. What do you look like Bolden? What kind of a man was he? Can you describe him physically?

items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26
items.q: He said, would you like to play with me? I said, very much so.

ctx.x: I said, King who is there? King Baldwin. Oh, I said, how are you, Mr. Baldwin, King?

He said, would you like to play with me? I said, very much so. I said, wait a minute. I ran back in the kitchen in the sister's back. I said, oh, that one made a wife. And boy, I was so happy. He said, no, you have to go back home and go to school. You promised your dad he was on the staff there in the 21. And when it was 21, 4 o'clock in the morning and 8 o'clock I was on the train. I've been gone ever since. Well, I was playing professionally, playing dances, you know. Oh, yeah, sure. That was about 18 then.…
How old were you, Ren Bold, and heard you?
